facts.statement: Anthropodyptes is a poorly known genus that contains only one species of extinct penguin.
facts.quote: Anthropodyptes is a poorly known monotypic genus of extinct penguin.

facts.statement: The only known species, Anthropodyptes gilli, is known from a Middle Miocene humerus found in Australia.
facts.quote: It contains the single species Anthropodyptes gilli, known from a Middle Miocene humerus from Australia.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Anthropodyptes might belong to the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae because its bones resemble those of the New Zealand genus Archaeospheniscus.
facts.quote: The bone is somewhat similar to those found in members of the New Zealand genus Archaeospheniscus and thus this genus might, like them, belong to the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae.

facts.statement: Anthropodyptes is classified within the family Spheniscidae.
Anthropodyptes lived between 23.04 and 15.98 million years ago during the Aquitanian to Burdigalian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Burdigalian (23.04 to 15.98 million years ago)
